strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the 120-product catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default DEFAULT_LIMIT=20, capped at MAX_LIMIT=50) and `offset` (default 0), returns `{ total, items }`, and refuses non-whole-number limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Tests start the real app in-process on an OS-chosen port and assert on the HTTP responses.
inScope: GET /products query `q`, `limit`, `offset` behaviour and the `total`/`items` response
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
The shop's search box UI (not in this repository)
assumptions: The real app runs in-process via createApp() on port 0, as test/products.test.js does; nothing is faked.

The catalogue is the fixed PRODUCTS list from src/catalogue.js (120 items, names like 'Kettle 1'..'Kettle 15'); expected names/counts are written from it, and DEFAULT_LIMIT/MAX_LIMIT are imported from src/app.js.
Results are in catalogue (id) order, as the code returns them; paging assertions rely on that.
Negative numbers and decimals count as 'not a whole number'; offset 0 and limit 1 are valid.
openQuestions: Should an empty `q=` behave like no `q` (the code lists everything)? Tested as listing everything.
Should an offset past the end return 200 with empty items (current behaviour) rather than an error?

risks.description: Case-insensitive match broken (e.g. only lowercasing one side), so the search box misses products
risks.mitigation: TC1 searches with upper-case and mixed-case q and checks exact total and names

risks.description: total reflects the page size instead of all matches, breaking pagination UI
risks.mitigation: TC3/TC4 assert total stays the match count while items is a slice

risks.description: Unbounded limit lets a client fetch the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC5 asserts limit above MAX_LIMIT returns exactly MAX_LIMIT items

risks.description: Invalid paging input yields 500 or silently odd results
risks.mitigation: TC7-TC9 assert 400 for each refused shape

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns only products whose name contains it, case-insensitively; without `q` every product is matched.
Results are paged by `limit` and `offset`, the response's `total` is the number of all matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
A `limit` or `offset` that isn't a whole number, or a `limit` below 1, is refused with 400.

testCases.title: matches product names containing q in any case
preconditions: App listening on an OS-chosen port
testCases.expected: 200, total 7, item names exactly Kettle 1, Kettle 10..Kettle 15
testCases.rationale: Proves substring + case-insensitive matching with an exact result set

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200, total 120, DEFAULT_LIMIT items starting at id 1
testCases.rationale: Default listing and default page size

testCases.title: returns no products and a total of 0 when nothing matches q
returns the page at offset with the total of all matches
testCases.rationale: Paging slice and total independent of page

testCases.title: caps a limit above the maximum at MAX_LIMIT items
returns an empty page but the full total when offset is past the last match
accepts limit 1 and offset 0 as the smallest valid values
refuses a limit that isn't a whole number or is below 1 with 400
steps: GET /products with limit = abc, 2.5, -1, 0 and empty (one parameterised test each)

testCases.title: refuses an offset that isn't a whole number with 400

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services; the app starts in-process on port 0. Runs under the existing `npm test` (vitest run).
